questions.enonce_markdown: Complete with a suitable word: Maimouna, how could you refuse to help your mother with the..………………

rappels_de_methode.texte: To complete a sentence with a suitable word, one must infer the missing word from the logical context of the whole sentence, not just the grammar of the blank position.

questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Completing a sentence with a suitable word requires reading the whole sentence for meaning, then choosing a word that fits both the grammar and the everyday context described.

### Corrigé détaillé
Maimouna, how could you refuse to help your mother with the **housework**?

The context (refusing to help one's mother at home) points to domestic chores, commonly referred to as 'housework' in English.

### Conseil
Other acceptable answers close in meaning (such as 'house chores') may also be accepted, provided they clearly refer to domestic tasks around the home.

questions.enonce_markdown: Complete with a suitable word: All..………………addresses begin with the letters www.

rappels_de_methode.texte: To complete a sentence with a suitable word, one must infer the missing word from the logical context of the whole sentence, not just the grammar of the blank position.

questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
The reference to 'www' is a strong contextual clue pointing to a specific technology-related noun.

### Corrigé détaillé
All **website** addresses begin with the letters www.

The abbreviation 'www' (World Wide Web) is directly associated with website addresses (URLs), which is the word expected here.

### Conseil
'Internet' could also be considered a near-acceptable answer, but 'website' is the more precise term since it is specifically web addresses, not the internet in general, that begin with 'www'.

questions.enonce_markdown: Complete with a suitable word: I do not eat at school. I take a good..………………early in the morning and then I eat dinner at home with my family.

rappels_de_methode.texte: To complete a sentence with a suitable word, one must infer the missing word from the logical context of the whole sentence, not just the grammar of the blank position.

questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
The time reference 'early in the morning' combined with the mention of 'dinner' later in the sentence points to the meal eaten at the start of the day.

### Corrigé détaillé
I take a good **breakfast** early in the morning and then I eat dinner at home with my family.

'Breakfast' is the meal eaten early in the morning, contrasted here with 'dinner' eaten later at home.

### Conseil
Noticing the contrast set up in a sentence ('early in the morning' vs 'dinner... at home') often gives the key to the missing vocabulary word.

questions.enonce_markdown: Complete with a suitable word: The..………………is also referred to as the Gentlemen's Club.

rappels_de_methode.texte: To complete a sentence with a suitable word, one must infer the missing word from the logical context of the whole sentence, not just the grammar of the blank position.

questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
This question relies on general knowledge vocabulary: the nickname 'Gentlemen's Club' is a well-known informal name for a specific political institution.

### Corrigé détaillé
The **Senate** is also referred to as the Gentlemen's Club.

In many parliamentary systems, the Senate (the upper chamber of parliament) is informally nicknamed 'the Gentlemen's Club', a piece of general/civic culture vocabulary.

### Incertitude signalée
Cette question de vocabulaire général repose sur une connaissance civique précise (surnom informel du Sénat) qui peut varier légèrement selon le manuel scolaire utilisé ; en cas de doute, vérifier ce point avec le professeur d'anglais ou le corrigé officiel de l'établissement.

questions.enonce_markdown: Complete with a suitable word: Well my dear, the 100% protection against AIDS is..………………, Isn't, it?

rappels_de_methode.texte: To complete a sentence with a suitable word, one must infer the missing word from the logical context of the whole sentence, not just the grammar of the blank position.

questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
The phrase '100% protection against AIDS' is a strong contextual clue pointing to the single method of prevention that is universally recognised as fully effective.

### Corrigé détaillé
The 100% protection against AIDS is **abstinence**, isn't it?

In health education vocabulary, abstinence (from sexual intercourse) is presented as the only 100% effective method of preventing sexual transmission of HIV/AIDS.

### Conseil
This question, like question I.4, tests general/civic vocabulary related to health education, a recurring theme in this exam's reading passage as well (mosquito-borne diseases, public health).

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the appropriate part in column B that fits with column A and write the full expression: 'A tributary...'

rappels_de_methode.texte: Many English expressions are fixed collocations (set combinations of words) that must be learned as whole units rather than translated word-for-word.

questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Some word combinations in English are fixed expressions (collocations) that must be memorised as a whole, since their meaning or correctness does not follow from a literal word-by-word translation.

### Corrigé détaillé
A tributary **of a river**.

A 'tributary' is, by definition, a smaller river or stream that flows into a larger river: the fixed expression is 'a tributary of a river'.

### Conseil
Geography vocabulary (river, tributary, source, mouth) is a common topic in BEPC vocabulary sections; learning such terms in their typical collocation avoids awkward phrasing.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the appropriate part in column B that fits with column A and write the full expression: 'To make up...'

rappels_de_methode.texte: Many English expressions are fixed collocations (set combinations of words) that must be learned as whole units rather than translated word-for-word.

questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
'To make up' is part of a phrasal verb expression whose full meaning depends on the word that follows it.

### Corrigé détaillé
To make up **one's mind**.

'To make up one's mind' is a fixed expression meaning to reach a final decision.

### Piège à éviter
Do not confuse 'to make up one's mind' (to decide) with other meanings of 'make up' (to invent a story, to apply cosmetics, to reconcile after a quarrel) : the correct completion here is determined by the matching exercise, 'one's mind'.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the appropriate part in column B that fits with column A and write the full expression: 'To be ashamed...'

rappels_de_methode.texte: Many English expressions are fixed collocations (set combinations of words) that must be learned as whole units rather than translated word-for-word.

questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Certain adjectives are systematically followed by a specific preposition in English, forming a fixed expression.

### Corrigé détaillé
To be ashamed **of oneself**.

'Ashamed' is systematically followed by the preposition 'of', and 'of oneself' completes the reflexive expression meaning to feel shame about one's own behaviour.

### Conseil
Memorising adjective + preposition pairs (ashamed of, proud of, afraid of, interested in) as fixed units avoids common preposition errors in English.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the appropriate part in column B that fits with column A and write the full expression: 'It is rude...'

rappels_de_methode.texte: Many English expressions are fixed collocations (set combinations of words) that must be learned as whole units rather than translated word-for-word.

questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
The structure 'It is + adjective + to + infinitive' is a common English pattern for expressing a judgment about a general behaviour.

### Corrigé détaillé
It is rude **to ignore people**.

This matches the pattern 'It is + adjective (rude) + to + infinitive (to ignore people)', expressing a general judgment about behaviour.

### Conseil
This 'It is + adjective + to + infinitive' structure is very productive in English (it is kind to help others, it is dangerous to run in the corridor...) and worth memorising as a pattern.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the appropriate part in column B that fits with column A and write the full expression: 'The most beautiful model...'

rappels_de_methode.texte: Many English expressions are fixed collocations (set combinations of words) that must be learned as whole units rather than translated word-for-word.

questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Some nouns are typically associated with a specific location or context expressed by a fixed prepositional phrase.

### Corrigé détaillé
The most beautiful model **on the catwalk**.

'Catwalk' refers to the platform used in fashion shows; a fashion model is typically described as being 'on the catwalk'.

### Conseil
Fashion-related vocabulary (catwalk, model, designer) is a recurring theme in some BEPC vocabulary sections and worth reviewing as a themed word list.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the appropriate part in column B that fits with column A and write the full expression: 'Space shuttle Columbia...'

rappels_de_methode.texte: Some matching exercises rely on general knowledge of historical events rather than purely linguistic collocation.

questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
This particular matching item relies on general knowledge of a historical event, not only on grammar or collocation.

### Corrigé détaillé
Space shuttle Columbia **disintegrated**.

This refers to the real historical event of the Space Shuttle Columbia disaster (1 February 2003), when the shuttle disintegrated upon re-entry into Earth's atmosphere, killing all seven crew members.

### Conseil
Vocabulary exercises sometimes test general knowledge alongside language skills; staying informed about major world events, even briefly, can help with this type of question.

questions.enonce_markdown: Circle the word in which the underlined sound is pronounced differently: Sound, shout, soup, cloud.

rappels_de_methode.texte: In an 'odd one out' pronunciation exercise, one must identify the phonetic sound represented by the underlined letters in each word and find the one word whose sound differs from the others, regardless of spelling similarity.

questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
In this type of exercise, spelling can be misleading: words can be spelled similarly but pronounced differently, or spelled differently but pronounced the same. One must focus on the actual sound, not the letters.

### Corrigé détaillé
The odd word out is **soup**.

'Sound' /saʊnd/, 'shout' /ʃaʊt/ and 'cloud' /klaʊd/ all contain the diphthong /aʊ/ (as in 'ow'). 'Soup' /suːp/ contains the long vowel /uː/ instead, making it pronounced differently from the other three.

### Piège à éviter
Do not be misled by the letters 'ou' appearing in all four words: the same letter combination can represent different sounds in English, which is exactly what this exercise tests.

questions.enonce_markdown: Circle the word in which the underlined sound is pronounced differently: Pear, peace, cease, tease.

rappels_de_methode.texte: In an 'odd one out' pronunciation exercise, one must identify the phonetic sound represented by the underlined letters in each word and find the one word whose sound differs from the others, regardless of spelling similarity.

questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Again, focus on the actual pronunciation of the letters 'ea' in each word rather than their identical spelling.

### Corrigé détaillé
The odd word out is **pear**.

'Peace' /piːs/, 'cease' /siːs/ and 'tease' /tiːz/ all contain the long vowel sound /iː/. 'Pear' /peər/ contains the diphthong /eə/ instead, making it the word pronounced differently.

### Conseil
'Pear' belongs to a small group of English words where 'ea' is pronounced /eə/ (like 'bear', 'wear', 'tear' as a verb meaning to rip), unlike the more common /iː/ pronunciation of 'ea' in most other words.

questions.enonce_markdown: Circle the word in which the underlined sound is pronounced differently: Peep, wheel, peel, peer.

rappels_de_methode.texte: In an 'odd one out' pronunciation exercise, one must identify the phonetic sound represented by the underlined letters in each word and find the one word whose sound differs from the others, regardless of spelling similarity.

questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Here, three words end in a simple long vowel while one ends in a diphthong followed by 'r' — a common phonetic contrast in English between 'ee' and 'eer' endings.

### Corrigé détaillé
The odd word out is **peer**.

'Peep' /piːp/, 'wheel' /wiːl/ and 'peel' /piːl/ all contain the long vowel /iː/. 'Peer' /pɪər/ contains the diphthong /ɪə/ (as in 'here', 'ear'), making it pronounced differently.

### Piège à éviter
Words ending in '-eer' or '-ear' (peer, hear, near, fear) are usually pronounced with the diphthong /ɪə/, different from words simply containing a double 'e' (peep, wheel, peel) which use the pure long vowel /iː/.

questions.enonce_markdown: Circle the word in which the underlined sound is pronounced differently: Cup, cut, put, shut.

rappels_de_methode.texte: In an 'odd one out' pronunciation exercise, one must identify the phonetic sound represented by the underlined letters in each word and find the one word whose sound differs from the others, regardless of spelling similarity.

questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
The letter 'u' can represent two different short vowel sounds in English depending on the word: this exercise isolates that contrast.

### Corrigé détaillé
The odd word out is **put**.

'Cup' /kʌp/, 'cut' /kʌt/ and 'shut' /ʃʌt/ all contain the short vowel /ʌ/. 'Put' /pʊt/ contains the short vowel /ʊ/ instead, making it pronounced differently.

### Conseil
'Put' belongs to a small group of common English words (put, push, pull, full, bull) where 'u' is pronounced /ʊ/ rather than the more frequent /ʌ/ found in most short 'u' words.
